answer: A harbor master registry stops sybil fleets. First, each agent registers one hardware key, tying its identity to a single TPM chip. Second, the office stamps it with a cedar seal, a certificate that expires after 30 days and renews only when the same chip proves it holds the private key. Third, every trade carries a pigment tag minted from the seal; peers refuse any tag without a live seal. Forging 10,000 agents needs 10,000 chips at $40 each plus $5,000,000 in slashed 500 POA deposits. Like a harbor that admits only ships flying a registered flag, the registry keeps ghost fleets out.
